analysis_notes.gap_analysis_narrative: Torah #236 is a single-paragraph practical teaching on rabbinic leadership. The text was read in full and examined line by line for bechina language ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', 'כנ"ל', or equivalent parallel-nature formulations). None was found. The teaching operates entirely in eitza (causal) logic: conducting rabbinic leadership with integrity and sincerity (רַבָּנוּת בְּכַשְׁרוּת וּבִתְמִימוּת) CAUSES / MERITS (זוֹכֶה) rising to greatness at the end of one's days. The example given — that in the current generation greatness means being regarded as a famous tzaddik — is an illustrative specification of the variable 'greatness,' not a bechina equation. The conclusion that the simple kosher man receives his reward (שְׂכָרוֹ) before leaving the world is a further causal consequence. Concepts mentioned in the Torah: רַבָּנוּת (rabbinic leadership), כַּשְׁרוּת (integrity/fitness), תְּמִימוּת (sincerity/wholeness), גְּדֻלָּה (greatness), כָּבוֹד (honor), צַדִּיק מְפֻרְסָם (famous tzaddik), אִישׁ כָּשֵׁר פָּשׁוּט (simple kosher person), שְׂכָרוֹ (his reward). All are joined by 'עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה' (through this he merits) and similar causal constructions — these are eitza connections only. No additions to torahData.js are warranted from this Torah.
